name: Claude Opus
why: I use Claude Opus to rip thru books. It points out the fluff paragraphs so I skip them.

quotes.quote: Every N issues I switch to opus and have it review the work done.
quotes.excerpt: I’m a solopreneur working on a fairly large number of independent projects. I use Claude Code to initiate a project using Sahil’s ME skill pack and write a high-level spec to a Linear ticket. If/when I’m ready to work on that idea, I convert it to a project, decompose the top ticket into more issues. I also have Claude code add to each issue with deepseek, sonnet or opus tags based on which is most appropriate for th
quotes.story: Ask HN: What is your (AI) dev tech stack / workflow? (June 2026)

quotes.quote: I only use the Claude Opus/Sonnet inside Windsurf after everything is crystal clear, or I want to let it handle tricky stuff
quotes.excerpt: Hey man, here's how to properly spend your 50 bucks and get the most bang for the $$: opencode go - $10 a month gets you decent allowance with latest GLM, MiniMax, and Kimi. Windsurf - $20 gives u access to nearlly all models. For me, I'm having these two subscriptions plus: shared Codex plans & shared Kimi coding Allegretto from Chinese resellers for around $10. I only use the Claude Opus/Sonnet inside Windsurf afte
quotes.story: Ask HN: $50 monthly budget, which coding models would you recommend now?

quotes.excerpt: I use Claude Opus to rip thru books. It points out the fluff paragraphs so I skip them. Finished stuff I prob never would've touched: Slaughterhouse Five, The Three-Body Problem. I make quick Anki cards from the Opus reading sessions so I don't forget plot bits. I try to get Opus to quiz me on the sections it told me to focus on reading.
